item.content:encoded:
People Who Don't Want To Seem Needy But Almost Always Do Usually Say 8 Things In Casual Conversation
Many people are painted as needy just for speaking their mind or asking for what they want. But those things aren't signs of anxious attachment.
But when someone's self-worth is tied to reassurance and they can't exist without someone wanting them, that's a problem. Usually, people are aware, but even those who don't want to seem needy still say certain things that make it seem that way, sabotaging their relationships in the process.
When people don't want to seem needy but usually do, they say these things
1. 'I didn't mean it'
Master of Stocks | Shutterstock
When someone's self-worth is tied up in another person's presence or attention, the boundaries they set can be quickly overstepped in the name of self-care. Someone who needs comfort to feel secure will quickly say "I didn't mean it" if it means avoiding the distress at hand.
Even if they're aware of their anxious attachment and are drained from trying to keep up with their need for constant reassurance, it's hard to break the cycle of over-apologizing when it's tied to anxious thoughts and insecurity.
2. 'I feel like you're upset'
Needy people may try to mask their need for reassurance with subtle questions like "Are you upset?" or "I feel like you don't like me, is that true?" While it might feel like the reassurance they're offered in response is a relief, excessively seeking it out only spirals into more loneliness and depression, even in a committed relationship.
We have to curate a sense of security in ourselves. Otherwise, we spend so much time and effort reading people's energy and trying to seek out their approval at our own expense.
3. 'You never texted me back'
Because social media and our phones are available all the time, it's easy for a needy person to rely on them for reassurance even after just a twinge of insecurity bubbles up. They get upset when their partners aren't immediately around or when they don't get a text back.
They're prone to reading into messages way too deeply, despite not having all the context. It's a hard cycle to break, but it's possible.
4. 'I'm being crazy'
Even if it's a direct response to assurance-seeking or over-apologizing, needy people are still asking for comfort from someone else when they say something self-critical like this. It has the same energy as "I'm just a terrible partner" or "you probably don't even want to be with me," toned down for effect.
At a certain point, their insecurities become an emotional burden on other people. They feel pressured to constantly reassure others, even if the only person who can really solve those insecurities is the one experiencing them.
5. 'I don't know what I'd do without you'
MDV Edwards | Shutterstock
While our social connections and relationships do highly influence our happiness and well-being, we shouldn't be dependent on others to feel secure. If our self-worth and sanity are completely tied up in someone else, we'll never truly feel good unless they're present and attentive, and that's impossible.
That's why needy people go through cycles of highs and lows, because they put too much stock in other people to shape how they feel about themselves. So, even if "I don't know what I'd do without you" feels somewhat harmless and sweet, in the hands of these people, it's a huge red flag.
6. 'Stop yelling at me'
Used in situations where someone's just expressing their emotions or concerns, needy people often guilt others into being similarly avoidant to protect their own peace. They can't handle anything but sheer validation and reassurance. Anything else feels like an inherently personal attack.
It's not surprising, considering their self-worth is tied to external perceptions and attention, but that doesn't mean it's healthy. And in highly emotional situations, they often can't help but resort to these defensive ways.
7. 'Are you mad at me?'
It's a classic phrase that needy people can't help but use, especially in close relationships and romantic situations where their mood is tied up in someone else. They try to control how someone else is feeling and read into their emotions all the time, because they don't feel a sense of control over their own internal state.
Even when the cue for a question like this is a change in someone's tone or a random choice of words, they can't help but let down their hypervigilance.
8. 'I'll fix it, I promise'
MDV Edwards | Shutterstock
An early clue for a needy person comes in the face of conflict. They may be aware of their own insecurities and dependent relationship habits, but they're really only committed to changing them for someone else's validation and presence.
As most of us know, that's a cycle that never truly helps anyone. And if someone's not self-aware or interested in leaning into discomfort, being forced to change because of someone else's request rarely creates the change they both need.
In a relationship that's tied to their self-worth, the stakes are high.
Zayda Slabbekoorn is a senior editorial strategist with a bachelor's degree in social relations & policy and gender studies who focuses on psychology, relationships, self-help, and human interest stories.

item.content:encoded:
Christina Haack has received another chance at love with Christopher Larocca.
After the pair were spotted on a joint trip to Italy in October 2024 followed by an appearance at Amy Sexton’s holiday party in Laguna Beach, California, in December 2024, Us confirmed in January 2025 that Haack was dating Larocca.
The couple went Instagram official in February 2025, going on to make their red carpet debut in May 2025.
Haack recently went through a public divorce from Hall in July 2024 after over two years of marriage.
“Everyone’s just doing better since he’s gone. Just all that negative energy,” she said during an episode of Christina on the Coast, referring to her children Taylor and Brayden whom she shares with ex Tarek El Moussa and son Hudson whom she shares with ex Ant Anstead. “I truly tried to make that work.”
Keep scrolling to learn more about Haack and Larocca’s relationship:
October 2024
The Daily Mail claimed that Haack and Hall were seen on a trip to Italy together.
December 2024
The pair were spotted at Sexton’s holiday party in Laguna Beach, per Daily Mail.
January 2025
Us confirmed that Haack was dating Larocca, who is the CEO of Network Connex in Orange County, California. Later that month, the couple were spotted at LAX traveling to Paris for Haack’s business trip.
February 2025
Haack and Larocca went Instagram official when she shared a photo of the pair flying on a private plane.
“Some plane flights must be hard,” she captioned the post.
That same month, Haack and Larocca went on a double date with Tarek and his wife, Heather Rae El Moussa.
“First round of interviews ✅,” Tarek shared in an Instagram post.
March 2025
Larocca appeared in the background of The Flip Off’s season finale.
April 2025
Haack shared in an Instagram post about anxious attachment that finding a man “who has his own amazing career, life & hobbies (who also happens to have zero jealousy) can at times feel strange for someone who has had the opposite.”
Later that month, Haack’s ex Tarek told Us that the “double dates” with Larocca and Haack are “actually fun.”
“The new guy she’s dating, I really like him. He’s really nice,” he shared. “Honestly, he just seems like a good guy. She’s going through a really tough situation and, based on my conversations with her, he’s supportive, he’s guiding, he’s experienced and he is giving her good advice.”
May 2025
The couple made their red carpet debut at The Flip Off For Your Consideration Emmy event in Los Angeles.
“A supportive partner > everything,” Haack shared via her Instagram Story.
September 2026
To mark two years of dating, Haack shared a heartfelt appreciation post for Larocca.
“Two years of getting to know you. Together we built a champagne brand from the ground up, partnered on a flip for tv (coming soon) and traveled to amazing places,” she wrote via Instagram on September 21. “I have watched you handle everything with grace and understanding and therefore you have taught me to do the same. Thank you for making my life EASY. What a true gift that is. A gift I would not have appreciated in my younger years. Taking things slow and not rushing through life is something I also can greatly appreciate in my 40s. Thank you for being a true partner in all the ways @cml949 🤍.”
